title: AI Spokesperson Video for Product Showcases | AIVideosUGC
description: Make an AI spokesperson video where an AI-generated person holds your product up to the camera and shows it from every side. Upload a product photo to try it.
h1: AI Spokesperson Video With a Person Holding Your Product
lead: An AI spokesperson video has an AI-generated person hold your product, turn it toward the camera, and show it off in a short clip. Add your message as captions after you download.
intro: An AI spokesperson video puts your product in someone's hands. An AI-generated person picks it up, holds it near their face or chest, turns it to show the label and the sides, and points to details like a strap or a cap. It gives shoppers a sense of size and makes the product feel like something people use every day.

Upload a product photo and write one sentence about the person and setting, such as “woman in a denim jacket holding the tote bag on a city sidewalk.” Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds in 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4. Add your message as typed captions after download.

benefits.d: Seeing the product in a hand shows how big it is better than a photo on a plain background.
Set the person and the place in your own words, from a home office to a park bench.
Keep the video focused on the product, then add your main points as on-screen captions before posting.

steps.t: Upload a photo of the product
steps.d: Pick a photo where the item stands alone and its full shape is visible.
Write who is holding it and where, for example “man in a gray hoodie at a kitchen table, holding the coffee bag.” Pick the size and length.

steps.t: Save it or change the scene
steps.d: Download the clip, or change the person or location in your sentence for another version.

uses.d: A vertical clip of someone showing the product feels at home among everyday creator posts.
Add it to the product gallery so shoppers get a feel for how big the item is in a hand.
Use a square cut in feed ads, where a person holding the item draws the eye to it.

faq.q: What does the person do in the video?
faq.a: They hold your product, turn it toward the camera, and show it from different sides. Describe the action in your sentence, like “lifts the bottle and taps the cap,” to guide the movement.

faq.q: Can I describe what the person looks like?
faq.a: Yes. Include details like age range, clothing, and setting in your description. Each video is generated separately, so the person may look different from one clip to the next.

faq.q: Is the person in the video real?
faq.a: No. Every person in these videos is AI-generated, not a real customer or creator, so don't present the clip as a genuine review. Some platforms require you to label realistic AI-generated content, so turn on the AI label wherever it's offered.

faq.q: Which products work well in these videos?
faq.a: Items that fit in one or two hands: skincare bottles, water bottles, phone cases, snack bags, headphones, and small purses. Large items like furniture are hard to show being held.

overview.h2: Let the person provide context, not a fake testimonial
overview.p: An AI spokesperson scene helps viewers judge scale and setting: a bottle beside a hand, a case near a phone, or a bag held at chest height. The person is a visual stand-in, not a customer or creator, so keep the message in typed captions you control.

overview.h2: Use a simple pose with one product focus
overview.p: Describe who is holding the item, where they are, and what their hands do. A single turn, lift, or point gives the product room to remain visible throughout the short clip.

input_guide.h2: Give the model a clear hand-sized reference

items.d: Choose a photo where the item is separate from other objects and its edges, handle, cap, or opening can be read.
A bottle, mug, case, pouch, or small bag is easier to place when the intended size is obvious from the product shape.
Name an age range, clothing color, and setting without asking the scene to carry a long script.
Say “turns the bottle toward the camera,” “lifts the pouch,” or “points to the strap,” then keep the pose simple.

items.t: Keep text out of the action
items.d: Put product names, offers, and feature sentences into typed captions after download so they remain accurate.
Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds for one AI-generated person to hold and show the product.
Use 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 depending on the placement you are preparing.

items.t: A cost visible before you run
items.d: The credit amount appears before generation and returns when a job fails.
The watermark-free download contains no spoken narration, music, or captions; add those in your own editing process.

after_download.h2: Add the message beside the product

items.d: Type product names, benefits, prices, and dates yourself because generated lettering may not stay exact.
Check that fingers, grip, product size, and label placement remain believable before using the file publicly.

items.t: Disclose the AI source where needed
items.d: If the publishing channel offers an AI-content label, turn it on and never frame the person as a genuine buyer.

fit.h2: Products that read well in a hand
good: Bottles, mugs, pouches, phone cases, headphones, and small bags
